do_not_assume: A matching model name guarantees an exposed route.
Authentication grants controller or entity access.
v1 and v2 have identical behavior.
An HTTP success proves the intended persisted state.
goal: A documented, least-privilege integration contract ready for safe testing.
steps: Record the target Rock environment and version.
Open the installed API v1 or v2 documentation.
Identify the exact controller, route, and operation.
Identify the caller’s session or REST Key without copying the secret into notes.
Classify the task as read-only, create, partial update, full replacement, or delete.
Inspect controller permissions and applicable entity security.
Define the smallest request and response fields.
Prepare a non-production or otherwise safe test record.
Define the independent readback and rollback expectation before sending a write.
Stop before production if unrestricted access is the only known way to make the call succeed.
title: Recipe: Preflight A REST Integration

do_not_assume: Store the token in an approved secret store, never public source or browser code.
goal: An active external credential with a named owner, bounded permissions, and a revocation plan.
steps: In the installed administration UI, navigate to REST Keys.
Create or locate a clearly named key for one integration purpose.
Add a description identifying its operational owner and use.
Verify the active state.
Grant only the controller operations the integration requires.
Store the token in an approved secret store, never public source or browser code.
Test the narrowest read operation first.
Test writes only after defining readback and rollback.
Record how the key will be revoked or replaced.

do_not_assume: `PUT` is safe for a partial object.
Omitted values are preserved by a full-update operation.
Do not retry the same full payload until omitted/defaulted properties are understood.
goal: Only the integration-owned fields are changed and independently verified.
steps: Confirm that the installed endpoint supports `PATCH`.
Read the target record and retain a bounded pre-write comparison.
Identify exactly which fields the integration owns.
Exclude navigation objects and unrelated properties unless their behavior is explicitly tested.
Submit the partial update against a safe record.
Read the entity back through a separate request or UI.
Compare the intended fields and confirm unrelated fields remain unchanged.
Stop if the endpoint normalizes, ignores, or changes properties unexpectedly.
Promote the pattern only after target-version validation.
Determine whether the integration used `PUT` or `PATCH`.
Inspect the installed operation help and current Model Map.
Compare the submitted payload with a pre-write snapshot.
Read the entity back through an independent path.
If the integration owns only selected fields, test the documented partial-update operation on a non-production record.
Do not retry the same full payload until omitted/defaulted properties are understood. (Intro to the Rock API)

Exercise valid, missing, malformed, unauthorized, and replayed requests in a safe environment.
Inspect logs without retaining secrets or unnecessary raw payloads.

Assume no default Lava-webhook security.

Identify every accepted query, form, header, cookie, and body value.

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: The exact endpoint work units, permissions, methods, and performance risks are understood before modification.
steps: Identify the Lava Application and every endpoint used by the client flow.

do_not_assume: Provider status has already been tied to the correct Rock record.

steps: List the provider event types with operational meaning.
Define the configured authenticity check for callbacks.
Define how each valid event correlates to a Rock communication, recipient, or person context.

Map events to concise operational states.
Build a bounded report or data view using the Rock-side communication fields needed by staff.
Exclude credentials, signatures, full raw bodies, and unrelated provider metadata.
Test a known event through receipt, correlation, state update, and report display.
Define an exception-review process for unmatched events.
Verify that the callback passed the provider’s configured authenticity check.
Determine whether it correlates to a Rock communication, recipient, or person context.

steps: Record the shipped Rock version and feature status.
